wrong: shame/noun oewn-07319716-n: In 'it will be quite a shame if he does not' the word is the speaker's own sympathetic regret - informal, gentle disappointment, never disgrace or reproach - which a learner who knows only the guilt sense will misread.

virtue/noun oewn-04856990-n: Moralising and gendered: applied almost only to women, it equates chastity with a person's whole goodness and makes its loss a fall ('a sister's sense of decency and virtue'), a euphemistic frame a learner must not use innocently.
buy/verb oewn-00685589-v: Chosen over 'believe' it casts the claim as a sales pitch and its believer as a possible dupe ('she bought his story'); sceptical, faintly dismissive of what is accepted.
elegance/noun oewn-04819517-n: A compliment word: to call something elegant is to approve of its taste, which is why Mr. Bennet's 'such an elegance to misfortune' works as irony; approving.
elegance/noun oewn-04819885-n: In science and mathematics an 'elegant' solution is high praise, not a neutral description of its shape; admiring.
